scope: Frozen eager-final-e23 and lazy receipt source copies, accepted shared current master adapter, matched optimized core commands, one ThinLTO paired probe, and correctness-only preflight. This review does not grant or qualify timing.

findings.result: Both optimized trees exactly match the previously source-reviewed and opt0 correctness-qualified eager/lazy copies. The lazy implementation, strict provenance, Taylor selection, row clearing, and proof-work/error harvesting have no new source changes. cfg(test)-only observation and tests remain excluded from normal optimized library builds.

The accepted receipt resolves one shared opt3 adapter artifact and binds its build record and prior selected-adapter source qualification. Both receipt cores explicitly link that identical artifact. Neither source tree calls private_select_f64; no native-batch or private-selected cfg is passed. default_master_backend therefore selects SymbolicaBatch, and the probe asserts that default before preparing cases. The unrelated opt-in selected native path is not activated by this experiment.

Both core commands use opt-level=3, codegen-units=16, embed-bitcode=yes, debuginfo=0, debug-assertions=no and overflow-checks=no. The probe uses the same flags plus lto=thin. Each command invokes the resolved hash-bound rustc and explicitly selects the resolved hash-bound linker. Both cores use CARGO_CRATE_NAME=iregi_rust while Rust crate names/metadata disambiguate eager and lazy. There is no arity2/binary-fold dependency, target-native, fast-math, panic-mode override, or numerical dependency rebuild. Retained numerical archives have their separately recorded original opt3/cgu1 profile.

The manifest carries all shared build input bindings, the accepted adapter/build/artifact chain, shared compiler log, compiler/linker executables, current source copies, prior receipt qualifications, scripts, and probe. The build requires a passed review bound to this manifest. It verifies frozen inputs and already-built outputs before and after each subsequent step and at completion; it retains terminal status and log hashes on failure. Exactly two core steps are capped at 180 seconds each and the ThinLTO probe step at 600 seconds, all on CPUs 6 and 7.

The probe retains the prior seven workload generators at singleton and batch32, including ordered complex Dual seeds. Every Snapshot equality includes represented input/output bits, context, basis, metadata, statuses, analytic/fallback flags, public statistics, diagnostics and four private proof counters. Both sides require inactive N5 certificate work. The no-argument path performs one cold, five repeated, and one final snapshot per implementation per case. The preflight runner rejects options, invokes the probe without --time, enforces 120 seconds, verifies exactly fourteen distinct expected pairs and fourteen snapshots, and rejects calibration output or a non-correctness completion mode.

The inherited fixed-41-pair timing code remains available only through the explicit --time branch. The current runner never supplies it and the manifest marks future timing authorized=false. This source review covers build and correctness admission only; it does not approve execution of calibration or timing blocks. The fixed_iterations text in correctness logs remains an unused label, not an executed correctness repetition count.

resolved_review_findings: The stale probe header now identifies eager-final versus lazy capture accurately.
Already-built core outputs are rehashed before the dependent probe link and during final verification.
The resolved compiler executable and shared compiler log are now explicitly hash-bound.
The resolved linker is both hash-bound and explicitly selected in all three frozen command lists.
